About Me

Operational Experience Meets Analytical Thinking

Sandeep Kumar Pulipati
Hyderabad, Telangana, India

I am a Business Operations and Seller Support professional with over 5 years of experience across seller support, escalation investigations, fulfillment-center operations support, and AI data quality evaluation. Since May 2022, I have worked at Amazon India across Selling Partner Support (SPS), T4 escalation investigations, and a PSAS operations support project, following earlier roles as an Analyst at Teleperformance (1 year 2 months) and a Business Development Executive at BharatPe (3 months).

My day-to-day work has centered on investigating why operational issues occur: reviewing multi-step case histories, researching Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), validating data quality, and documenting findings clearly under strict SLA targets. Moving into data analytics is a practical extension of this work—using Excel, SQL, Power BI, and Python to summarize operational metrics, spot recurring bottlenecks, and support data-informed decisions.

I bring strong real-world habits in process compliance, root-cause investigation, and basic Excel reporting, while actively building my foundational technical skills in SQL, Power BI, and Python through hands-on portfolio projects.

Transferable Analytical Strengths

  • • Issue Investigation: Reviewing case histories, logs, and policy guidelines to identify root causes of seller and fulfillment problems.
  • • Data Tagging & Quality Review: 14 months of validating AI outputs, categorizing defects, and applying quality rubrics at Teleperformance.
  • • Process & SLA Discipline: Resolving high-volume queues (35–40+ cases/day) while maintaining 90%–95% resolution rates and clear documentation.

Portfolio Projects

Data Analytics Projects

Practical analyses built around operational support questions. Projects 1, 2, and 4 are completed and verified on a simulated 250-row dataset; Project 3 is planned with its DAX specification ready.

Simulated Dataset Note: All projects use a simulated 250-row synthetic e-commerce support ticket dataset (synthetic_operations_tickets_250rows.csv) created for learning and demonstration. No data from Amazon or any other employer is used.
01 • Excel Operations Dashboard Completed

Excel Operations & SLA Performance Analysis

Objective: Structure a 250-ticket support log in Microsoft Excel, classify SLA breaches using helper formulas, and summarize resolution performance across issue categories and support tiers.

Dataset: Simulated 250-row synthetic e-commerce support ticket log (learning & demonstration).
Tools Used: Microsoft Excel (IF, COUNTIF, COUNTIFS, AVERAGEIF, KPI summary tables, column chart).
Verified Key Findings (n = 250)
  • Overall SLA compliance is 85.6% (214 within SLA, 36 breached) with an average resolution time of 18.8 hours and a 96.8% QA pass rate (242/250).
  • Tier 2 Operations Support is the primary bottleneck at 77.8% SLA compliance (35/45 within SLA, 31.5 hrs avg), compared to 89.2% in Tier 1 and 83.3% in Tier 4.
  • Fulfillment & Warehouse Discrepancy (28.2 hrs avg, 80.0% SLA) and Account Policy Escalations (28.9 hrs avg, 82.2% SLA) require the longest turnaround.
02 • SQL Case Analysis Completed

SQL Business & Operations Case Analysis

Objective: Query the relational support_tickets table in SQLite to evaluate ticket volume distribution, turnaround times, and First Contact Resolution (FCR) outcomes.

Dataset: Simulated 250-row synthetic support ticket table in SQLite (support_tickets).
Tools Used: SQL / SQLite3 (SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, CASE WHEN, COUNT, AVG, ROUND).
Verified Key Findings (n = 250)
  • Order Status Inquiries resolve fastest at 7.1 hours average with 91.5% SLA compliance (47 tickets), followed by Listing & Catalog Updates (13.6 hrs avg, 88.9% SLA).
  • Payment & Settlement Clarification represents the highest category volume (58 tickets, 86.2% SLA, 15.6 hrs avg).
  • Tier 1 General Support handles 55.6% of total ticket volume (139/250 tickets) while maintaining 89.2% SLA adherence.
03 • Power BI Performance Dashboard Planned

Power BI Service Operations Dashboard

Objective: Design an interactive single-page Power BI Desktop report enabling operations leads to filter SLA compliance, ticket backlog, and QA pass rates by support tier, priority, and region.

Dataset: Simulated 250-row synthetic support ticket dataset (synthetic_operations_tickets_250rows.csv).
Tools Planned: Power BI Desktop, Power Query data cleaning, foundational DAX measures (COUNTROWS, DIVIDE, CALCULATE).
Project Status & Prepared Scope
  • Honest Status: Labeled as Planned while the interactive Power BI Desktop (.pbix) report view is being finalized.
  • Core DAX measure definitions and report wireframe layout are prepared and available for inspection in the project specification.
04 • Python Data Analysis Completed

Python Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

Objective: Use Python (pandas and matplotlib) to validate data completeness, compute grouped operational summaries, and plot tier SLA performance against the 85.0% benchmark.

Dataset: Simulated 250-row synthetic support ticket dataset (learning & demonstration).
Tools Used: Python 3, pandas (read_csv, isnull, groupby), matplotlib.
Verified Key Findings (n = 250)
  • Confirmed 0 missing values across all 11 columns and 250 ticket records.
  • First Contact Resolution (FCR = 'Yes') was achieved on 57.6% of tickets (144/250).
  • Visual benchmark comparison shows Tier 1 (89.2%) exceeds the 85.0% SLA target, while Tier 4 (83.3%) and Tier 2 (77.8%) fall below the target line.
